### 2026-10-26: # Started researching Ideas

**5.1h**

# Started researching Ideas

So after designing the curtain opener for my week 1 and 2 projects, I figured that it would be good to continue in the same direction, and try to make something else automated. Then I decided, why not make the thing that automated everything.

So I decided to make a SmartHome Dashboard and controller.

## The Plan

I want to use an E-ink display, as they look really fancy, and are meant to be really low power. I'll use some sort of MCU to control it, probably an esp32s3, so it could be used standalone if needed. However, I plan to also include some sort of SBC capable of running something like home assistant.

So my original plan was to make it fully solar powered, but after finding out the battery draw of SBC's, I've come to the annoying conclusion that the solar power will have to be a backup, or at least supplemented with mains. Also would like to make the solar panel track the sun, but unsure if I will have the budget for this.

## My progress
### E-Ink
Have been researching parts that I can use.

Originally wanted to go with this screen:

![10466](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/9a5ff8f9b38b02ecf266bc8385b4acb0611a2b4038632406cc60892ba8e4a0c6.png)

This looked good, as $26 is manageable, and I also thought that 3 colour would be good - and the size and resolution is really good - 7.5" at 880x528.

But it has a problem. I'm pretty sure that it will have a much slower refresh rate than a standard bw one, and it will draw much more power as it has to cycle the red out.

So currently I don't know what e ink screen I'll get, but I have this one as a backup.

### SBC's

Due to AI, I guess, SBC's are all stupidly expensive. But I ideally want something that can run home assistant, as I don't fancy trying to code my own. Obviously looked at RPis first, but they're too expensive. But the Pi Zero 2 W, looked interesting, as it's meant to be a really cheap, barely SBC board.

but...

Yup, you say the price. A whole $91 for something less powerful than my 2nd gen intel CPU. That was surprising. tbh, didn't realise quite how good 2nd gen intel actually still is.

le potato...?

I spoke to someone I know who knows electronics, and he suggested an older used rpi board. so I looked at it, and I could actually get a raspberry pi 3 B 1gb model...

### 2026-10-27: # Found a Solar Panel

**1.7h**

# Found a Solar Panel

Started researching them a while ago. But finally found a solar panel I was happy with.

## My tangent with bare cells

So from research, I read that managing bare solar panels is a slight pain, as the voltage can fluctuate a lot. But I was willing to give it a try. So I looked at bare cells:

![10599](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/a14ce0983a036f86b7c5921f84b297c0ff4aef12a646c60eea33680c37d5b950.png)

~$9 for a single 5w 5v panel seemed steep, but it is what it is, so then I looked into MPPT boards, which seemed complex, but not too bad. So I found one in the end that I was happy with.

Then I looked again at solar panels and realised I can just get the phone charging ones. That dont need extra boards

## The result

I'm now planning to get a 30W, yes 30W panel - still monocrystalline, but it will output a stable 5v through usb. Not really sure how this will work, as I thought USB-A only went up to 18W. But we'll have to see. Worse case I just cut the wires a bit.

![10598](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/3f7db29ce2833b32e4449fb8e7f3a0758e9a0395c045858de9c96a021499f75c.png)

And it's also fairly cheap, at $14 - which is less than the bare panel and charging circuitry needed for the bare panel route.

So anyway, I'll have to charge that into an 18650 charging module, and I'll also try to put like a MOSFET in, so I can cap the charge when the battery hits 80%.

But having a 30W panel should make it quite quick.

## tl;dr

Figured out a pre made solar panel charging setup would be more cost effective, and have somehow ended up with a 30w panel.

### 2026-10-27: # Found a Screen

**4.2h**

# Found a Screen

So I always knew for this week that I wanted to use some sort of E ink display. This is as their low power capabilities and supposed paper printing like crispness have intrigued me.

## My mishaps

So before I researched any other parts, I did have a gander to see what the market was like. And to my suprise, I found this:

![10619](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/59cb3bc078d992f6f8944c828ab18e337f9505954e5dd1ef8bcc09f16ae4d0b9.png)

A 7.5" 880x528 black white and even red e ink display for only $26. Well this is still a pretty good deal.

Then, as I was still looking, possibly for even cheaper or better screens, I found this one:

![10621](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/28dd4f4b70dc42adf2521a65567a1742cad06fcb0533403f7184ca97acf0ac53.png)

Some random black white I think e reader e ink display, for only $15. It was only 6" though, but seemed to have a really high ppi, at least in the photo, as I don't think I found a resolution spec.

## My realisations

So as I was looking for what would be needed to run a bwr display, and it turns out, they're actually very useless for any sort of refresh rate. Than bummed me out a bit, as I'd just started thinking of how I could use red as an accent. But that basically meant sticking to bw displays to I could have decent screen refreshes which won't trigger epilepsy lol.

Oh and I realised both were bare boards, so id have to figure out correctly which driver boards they'd both use, and how to wire everything.

## So more research

So was just looking for cheap e ink displays, and couldn't actually find any 7" + ones annoyingly.So I decided to downsize and look for 5.8" ones. Even less options there.

Then I finally went down to 4.2". Guess what the best option was:

![10620](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8e9b36c32a45b67225189e50e409f732dbfbece6a92e68f75f72bccbb4e9f630.png)

Annnnddd... it's black white and red. But 4.2" and only $15! Although would need to get a driver as well

But on the upside, there's a store called WeAct which sells e ink displays which a lot of people seem to buy - they had the top sales thing on AliExpress. And they also come pre integrated with a display driver board thing. So looking there, I found a 3.7" E ink.

![10622](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/a9028b999886ae8266fe90933b54f6a9eb2e5abc6adda986d346146d1d9038cb.png)

So for $17.38, it's a very reasonable price, and the like sub second partial refresh rate is very nice. Butttt... 3.7" Thats gotta be too small.

So I spent even more time looking - across websites as well, with waveshare looking promising, until I got to a $12 shipping fee. That's the price of the board!!

So I ended up back on AliExpress, and found a 4.2" one. So a tiny bit better

![10618](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/f228d3286a83b47cacc1b9eadbfdfb4ca8db5c715601a07c249a156d13e7e259.png)

And at $23, it'll fit in budget. And for now, $23 for the screen and the driver hardware, is something I think has a decent price to performance.

## tl;dr

Looked through quite an interesting assortment of E ink displays - I assume the black white red ones are surplus shop displays - and have now ended up on an AliExpress 4.2" bw 400x300 screen.
